role: The server's connection list: binds the LAN TCP endpoint and the local endpoint, and each server tick drains every connection's received packets, dropping dead ones.
scope_reason: Wire format and connection plumbing: native messages are structs by design (SPEC: messages are structs, not bytes) (triage 2026-09-25, out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md).

members.name: eventLoops
members.note: Static Netty thread pool; the native tick is single-threaded.

members.name: mcServer
members.note: Back-reference; the native serverreplay struct fills this role.

members.name: endpoints
members.note: The bound channels; the native engine has one fixed connection.

members.name: networkManagers
members.note: The live connections; the native engine has the one server player.

members.name: addLanEndpoint
members.note: TCP listener; unused in-process (the pipeline it builds includes the ping responder and the encoders).

members.name: addLocalEndpoint
members.note: The LocalServerChannel the integrated server client connects to; the native join replaces the handshake.

members.name: networkTick
members.note: Per connection: processReceivedPackets and dead-connection cleanup. The native tick's deliver phase is the single-connection equivalent; the disconnect and crash-report branches have no counterpart.

missing: The endpoint lifecycle (bind, terminate, dead-connection removal with onDisconnect): the native engine has one fixed in-process connection and no disconnect path.
notes: The local endpoint's ChannelInitializer attaches no timeout, encoder or ping handlers, only the packet handler, which is why the in-process connection carries no byte layer at all.
